political-status.description: The political condition or status attributed to the polity in the source

Institutions such as Parliament or Congress
include: The American colonies when discussed collectively
Political communities assigned interests, duties, or capabilities

authorial-assessment.description: The source's explicit assessment of the system

stated-purpose.description: The purpose or justification attributed to the system

A country governed by the system
include: Monarchy, hereditary succession, republic, and representative government

claimed-authority.description: The authority the institution claims or is assigned

institution-type.description: The institution's governmental, legislative, or religious role

categories.definition: A named governing, legislative, religious, or representative body that exercises or contests authority.

An informal class of unnamed supporters
include: Named collective bodies with institutional powers

Named doctrines and paired political alternatives
Principles whose meaning or consequences recur across sections
